title: Stream-fence latency driving GPU page pin growth during continuous batching
creator: Maya Patel
description: Production clusters running sustained continuous-batching workloads show steady GPU RSS growth correlated with long-latency cudaEvent/sync fences between inference streams. Symptoms: gradual increase in device-resident pages (nvidia-smi RSS) across nodes over hours, increased fragmentation, and occasional OOMs under peak QPS. We can reproduce on staging with a synthetic workload that issues mixed sequence-length requests and aggressive KV cache prefetching. The allocator (cudaMallocAsync + multipool) appears to hold slabs because host-side frees are delayed until stream events are signalled; when event latency spikes (driver/PCIe or kernel scheduling), frees pile up and slab coalescence fails, leaving many small resident fragments and pinned staging buffers. This ticket tracks a deep-dive, hypotheses, mitigations, and a short-term patch to apply to runtime-1.29.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Maya Patel: Initial alert from ops: node-12 reported RSS increase ~1.4GB over 12h while throughput steady. Attached nvidia-smi snapshots and sample prometheus series (gpu_rss_bytes). Opening investigation; assigning to Diego.

2026-03-02 - Diego Ramirez: Reproduced on staging with continuous-batch harness (seeded workload: mix of 8/256/1024 token requests, batcher target latency 40ms). Observed cudaEvent latencies occasionally >200ms on worker stream in perf traces from perfetto. nvprof timeline shows a backlog of pending deallocations waiting for events on non-default streams.

2026-03-03 - Diego Ramirez: Hypothesis #1: cudaMallocAsync's deferred free queue is gated by stream event completion; when events are delayed (host CPU preemption, kernel stalls), pool residency increases. Hypothesis #2: our KV cache prefetch uses a custom stream-per-request pattern that creates many short-lived streams/events that prevent slab coalescing due to interleaved ownership.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy staging runtime-1.28 with debug allocator flags (ENV: ALLOC_DEBUG=1, TRACE_EVENTS=1) to a 4-GPU node. 2) Run continuous-batch harness: 60 batcher workers, request mix configured in /harness/configs/cont-batch-mix.yaml. 3) Collect perfetto traces and run 'nvidia-smi dmon' continuous sampling. 4) Observe gpu_rss_bytes increasing steadily and trace sections where cudaEventQuery/cudaStreamSynchronize latencies spike.
data_observations: - Perfetto: clusters of deferred_free calls pile up during 2-10s windows. - Prometheus: gpu_rss_bytes increases ~100-200MB per hour on affected nodes. - Memory histogram: fragmentation increases (many small free chunks <64KB). - Kernel traces: intermittent host-side scheduling delays coinciding with event completion latencies.
hypotheses_and_risks: 1) Deferred frees gated by delayed event completion causing slab retention; risk: long-term RSS drift leading to OOM. 2) Stream-per-request pattern prevents memory reuse across streams causing tiny orphan fragments; risk: fragmentation amplifies under mixed sequence lengths. 3) Misused cudaMemPoolSetAttribute or lack of pool trim allows resident pages to remain; risk: harder to reclaim without application restart.
short_term_mitigation_proposal: - Add config toggle: ALLOC_DEFER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5000) that forces reclamation of deferred frees older than timeout by issuing a lightweight cudaStreamSynchronize on owner stream in background worker (safe-mode only). - Add telemetry: sample deferred_free queue lengths per pool and expose in console dashboard. - Update job on runtime-1.29-canary with toggle enabled for 24h to validate reduction in RSS growth.
long_term_changes: - Rework KV prefetch stream strategy to use a small pool of long-lived streams instead of one-per-request to enable consistent ownership and better coalescing. - Implement slab coalescer that attempts cross-stream merge after event completion using per-slab epoch markers. - Investigate integrating cudaMemPoolTrim or calling cudaMemPoolSetAttribute(MEMPOOL_ATTR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD) during low-util windows.
next_steps: 1) Diego to land minimal telemetry + ALLOC_DEFER_TIMEOUT_MS on runtime-1.29-canary (ETA 3 days). 2) Run 72h canary with heavy mixed-length workload; collect perfetto + prometheus. 3) If RSS growth reduced >80% and no latency regressions, schedule rollout to one hostpool. 4) Parallel spike: implement stream-pool experiment and compare fragmentation metrics.
